test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the primary reason for the heating effect in a conductor when an electric current passes through it?

options.text: The movement of protons causes heat generation.
The electric field in the conductor causes heat generation.
The movement of electrons causes heat generation.
The conductor absorbs heat from the surrounding environment.

solution:
The correct answer is __The movement of electrons causes heat generation.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Heating effect__ in a conductor occurs due to the resistance offered to electron movement.
 
• When electrons move through the conductor, they collide with atoms, creating thermal energy.
 
• The resistance of the conductor is a key factor in determining the amount of heat generated.
 
• Energy is dissipated in the form of heat due to Joule’s law of heating.
 
• The heating effect is proportional to the square of the current, resistance, and time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Field:**

 
 
• Electric fields within the conductor guide the electrons but do not directly cause heat generation.
 
• They play a role in initiating the movement of charges.
 
 
 
• **Protons:**
 
 
• Protons are stationary within the atomic structure and do not contribute to the heating effect.
 
• The movement of free electrons is responsible for heat generation.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Heat:**
 
 
• The surrounding environment may affect the temperature but does not cause the heating effect due to current flow.
